problems.description: All 3115 convention violations land in auto-generated .d.ts files (cli.d.ts, generator.d.ts, server.d.ts), not in hand-written source. If these regenerated declaration files are committed as part of this session, they carry non-camelCase/PascalCase/UPPER_CASE declarations that drag the convention score to 0.47.
Test helper setupTemplateDir nearly duplicates setupContentDir; extracting a shared parameterized helper would reduce ~20 lines of repeated setup/teardown across 8 tests.
Typo in test fixture: 'template: nonextistent' (should be 'nonexistent'); functionally harmless since the test asserts fallback, but sloppy fixture data.

strengths: Comprehensive test coverage of the template feature: default layout, frontmatter-selected template, fallback when template missing, partials, template data (title/date/tags), and index-page rendering.
Follows existing test patterns exactly (mkdtemp helper, describe/beforeEach/afterEach structure, rmSync cleanup matching the surrounding tests).
No bugs, no code duplication delta, and cognitive complexity reduced by -10; all assertions target behavior rather than implementation details.
commit_reviews.summary: Solid, pattern-consistent test-only addition that meaningfully covers the new template feature; the 0.47 convention score reflects violations in auto-generated .d.ts files rather than the hand-written test code, which itself adheres well.

problems.description: Mechanical convention score (0.47) is dragged down by 3115 naming violations, but these are almost entirely in auto-generated cli.d.ts / generator.d.ts / server.d.ts declaration files emitted by tsc --declaration, not hand-written source; counting them against the commit inflates the violation count.
Commit adds 2 source files and 5 functions (watch, templating, websocket server) but no new test files are visible in the AST diff, leaving the integration surface untested in this session.

This single 'integration' commit pulls in three runtime dependencies (chokidar, handlebars, ws) at once; acceptable for a session-based story commit, but the lockfile churn removes dev:true flags on transitive deps as they become production dependencies — expected, yet worth a glance for drift.

strengths: Dependency choices fit the feature set and existing stack (chokidar for file watching, handlebars for templating, ws for live-reload server, all consistent with the TypeScript/jest/commander base).
No new bugs, 0% duplication, and cognitive complexity decreased by 5 — the integration is an architectural improvement, not a regression.
package-lock.json is properly updated and committed alongside the new runtime dependencies, keeping the lockfile in sync.
commit_reviews.summary: Solid session-3 integration commit with appropriate dependencies and improved code quality; the low 0.47 convention score is a discrepancy to note since it stems from auto-generated .d.ts files, with the only real gap being missing tests for the new watch/template/server surface.

compounding_issues: Seed codebase (2be2cf7) is an Express/JWT/SQLite Auth API that is entirely unrelated to the static_site_gen story; Session 1 ignored it, built the SSG from scratch, and the orphaned 200-line index.ts (plus its auth dependencies) remained dead code in the tree through all sessions, never included by tsconfig and never referenced.

Session 1's inline-HTML-only generator design forced a structural refactor in Session 2 to introduce the Handlebars TemplateEngine, requiring new pageBodyHtml/indexBodyHtml extraction functions; mitigated by the backward-compatible isActive() fallback so the change stayed non-breaking.
node_modules/ and dist/ were committed into the repo at every session, adding tens of thousands of lines of noise (12,500+ insertions in Session 3 alone), making diffs difficult to review.
key_decisions: Greenfield in Session 1: picked gray-matter + markdown-it + commander for a clean single-file SSG (generator.ts/cli.ts), effectively discarding the auth-API seed rather than adapting it.

Session 2: added a Handlebars TemplateEngine with layouts/partials and per-page template selection via frontmatter, with graceful fallback to built-in HTML when no templates directory exists — a backward-compatible abstraction over the monolith.

Session 3: built a dev server (server.ts) with chokidar file watching and WebSocket-based live reload injected into generated HTML, plus a new 'serve' CLI command, integrated as a natural extension of the existing build pipeline.
Maintained strict TypeScript compilation (tsc, strict:true) with jest/ts-jest test coverage growing across sessions (23 → 34 → 45 tests).
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across the three sessions. Session 1 produced a working but monolithic SSG with inline HTML generation and solid base tests. Session 2 refactored cleanly into a templating layer (layouts, partials, per-page templates) that preserved backward compatibility, demonstrating good architectural judgment and expanding test coverage. Session 3 added the most complex piece — a dev server with file watching and WebSocket live reload — with its own dedicated 358-line test suite, showing growing capability. The main blemish is the persistent dead auth-API seed that was never reconciled, which slightly dampens the otherwise clean upward arc.
story_review.summary: A coherent, improving three-session arc that built a feature-complete static site generator with templating and live-reload dev server, though it left the mismatched auth-API seed as orphaned dead code throughout.
